newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece tells U.S. it will fight video piracy.
newsitem.headline: Greece tells U.S. it will fight video piracy.

text.p: Greece has presented a plan to the United States detailing steps it will take to stop widespread piracy of copyright material for television, records and computer software, a statement issued by the U.S. embassy here said on Tuesday.
It said past efforts by Greece had been inadequate, prompting Washington to make a special review of Greece's case.
U.S. trade representative Charlene Barshefsky said that an April 30 deadline had been set for implementing the measures. Greece will remain on the priority watch list during this time.
"I now look forward to full implementation of the Action Plan and satisfactory resolution of U.S. copyright concerns by April 30, 1997," she said in the statement.

The United States has blamed Greek piracy for losses of $102 million in 1995. About 60 percent was motion picture rights and 40 percent sound recordings, computer programmes and business or entertainment software.

Since the liberalisaton of Greek television and radio in the late 1980s, scores of channels and stations have been opened. The leading television channels have joined U.S. companies in trying to stamp out piracy.
But smaller channels routinely broadcast unauthorised or pirated material. The dispute is a leading source of friction between the two countries.
A number of U.S. copyright holders have called on Washington to raise Greece to the priority foreign country list, which could lead to trade sanctions.
